chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from [Yunus], from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

Al-Khattab al-Awr asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and I was seated there, so he said: 'There was a hired worker with my father who worked for him for wages. So we lost him, and there remained for whom we lost him, and there remained for him something from his wages, and we do not know an heir for him.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'So seek him.' He said: 'We have sought him, but we did not find him.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Poor' – and he moved his hands (gestured).

He (the narrator) said, 'So I repeated to him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Seek and strive. If you can find him, [keep it for him]; otherwise, it is like your wealth until there comes to him a claimant.'
So if death befalls you, bequeath with it that if a claimant comes to him, then it should be handed over to him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the wages of a lost worker with no known heirs in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential procedure for handling the wages of a hired worker who is lost (mafqud) with no known heirs. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs the employer to diligently search for the worker; if unsuccessful, the wages are retained by the employer as a trust (amanah) until a claimant appears, mirroring the status of the employer's own wealth, and should be bequeathed if the employer passes away before the worker is found. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on preserving the rights of the absent party through active effort and secure custodianship rather than immediate distribution.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Hisham Bin Salim who said,

‘Khatab Al-Awr asked Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), and I was seated there, so he said, ‘There was an employee with my father who worked for him for the wages. So we lost him, and there remained for him something from his wages, and we do not recognise his inheritors’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So seek him’. He said, ‘We have sought him, but could not find him’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Poor’ – and he<sup>asws</sup> moved his<sup>asws</sup> hands (gestured).

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I repeated to him<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Seek and strive in accordance to your ability, or else it is like your wealth until there comes someone seeking it.
So if there befalls with you what befalls (death), so bequeath with it that if someone comes seeking it, then it should be handed over to him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from [Yunus] from Hisham ibn Salim who has narrated the following: “

Khattab al-A‘war asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when I was sitting, ‘A man worked on hire with my father and we lost him. A certain amount from his wages was left with us and we did not know any of his heirs.
He (the Imam) said, ‘You must search for him.’ He said, ‘We searched but did not find him.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘Destitute people’, making a hand gesture with his both hands.
The man repeated his question. He (the Imam) said, ‘Search and try hard if you can find him, otherwise, it is like your other assets until someone comes asking for it;
and if something happens to you, make a will about it to give it to the one who may come asking for it (remaining wages).”’
